summary: The reference patch (solution/fix.patch applied by solution/solve.sh) implements every rule in SOP TM-07 sections 2-8. Where the SOP gives no rule (no blank result, a run without a CCV on both sides, or a spike or parent that is a non-detect), it keeps the shipped calculation, as instruction.md:5 requires. All patch hunks match the shipped files line for line. No concrete incorrect behavior was found.
checks_performed: Checked that the manifest's 21 files, plus the manifest itself, are the files read; all were read in full.

Checked that every fix.patch hunk header and its context lines match the shipped sources: blanks.py lines 1-8, calib.py lines 9-17, qc.py lines 6-21, report.py lines 15-21, 30-35, 38-43 and 60-65, samples.py lines 6-18. patch -p1 from / resolves a/app/src/... to /app/src/..., and the Dockerfile installs patch and copies app/ to /app.
SOP 2: the patched fit_line uses the mean-centred OLS slope and intercept mean_y - slope*mean_x (fix.patch:27-32), not the origin-forced fit.
SOP 3: calib.reading is (response - intercept)/slope and is left unclamped (calib.py:17-19).

SOP 4: the patched blank_level averages blank readings >= mdl from all blanks in any position (fix.patch:11-13). With no blank result it keeps the shipped first-blank reading, or 0.0 when there is no blank (blanks.py:6-9).

SOP 5: amount is (reading - level)*dilution (fix.patch:107-108). The flag is judged on corrected(reading, level) with ND below mdl, J from mdl up to but not including loq, and an empty flag at or above loq (fix.patch:113-119). value is null only for ND (report.py:46).
SOP 5, exact limits: the flag and the detected test both use the same samples.corrected expression (fix.patch:88, 113), so a value landing exactly on mdl or loq is judged the same way in both places.

SOP 6: ccv_passes is 90.0 <= round(recovery,1) <= 110.0, and the reported recovery is unrounded (fix.patch:44, report.py:27-30). SOP 1 excludes near-ties, so Python round-half-even cannot change a graded result.
SOP 6 bracketing: with CCVs on both sides, ccv_ok requires the nearest CCV on each side to have passed. Otherwise the shipped nearest-CCV-before-else-True logic stays (fix.patch:49-56).

SOP 7: when spike and parent are both results (corrected >= mdl), recovery is (spike_amount - parent_amount)/added*100. Otherwise the shipped /(added*dilution) formula stays, applied to the SOP-5 amounts, so the recovery is always a number (fix.patch:60-63, 96).
SOP 8: the report keeps its structure, run order and analyte order. blank_levels is keyed by analyte name, and no rounding is applied (report.py:13-66).
The driver tools/metalquant_run.py is untouched by the patch, as instruction.md:3 requires.

Cross-checked the patched package against solution/model.py, which was written independently from the SOP. The branching agrees for every rule; I used this as corroboration only, not as proof of correctness.
Checked division safety: slope > 0 and at least two distinct concentrations give sxx > 0, added > 0, and CCV true values are positive (SOP 1).
Checked that amounts are filled in for every sample and spike before the spike loop, and that a parent is always an earlier sample (SOP 1), so the amounts and detected lookups for parents succeed.

coverage_sweep.category: Trace an ordinary case and each relevant boundary through the reference logic
coverage_sweep.reason: Traced these cases through the patched code: ordinary samples; mdl and loq boundaries; mdl == loq; negative readings; zero, one and several blank results; blanks before and after samples; dilutions 1 to 1000; CCV pass and fail at the rounded 90.0 and 110.0 edges; bracketed, one-sided and no-CCV runs; spikes with both, one or neither of spike and parent as results.

coverage_sweep.category: Output bytes: widths, precision, delimiters, paths
coverage_sweep.reason: The report is JSON printed by the unchanged driver. The SOP forbids rounding and the reference rounds nothing; round() is used only for the pass decision. Key names and the null value for ND match SOP 8.

coverage_sweep.category: State-updating branches (loop state, replacement, identifier reuse)
coverage_sweep.reason: amounts, detected and ccv_pass are dicts keyed by distinct run ids (SOP 1 guarantees distinct ids). bracket_ok recomputes the before and after lists for each index, so no state carries over between iterations.
The task is a pure batch computation with no persistence or interruption semantics.

coverage_sweep.category: SOP-silent fallbacks keep the shipped calculation (instruction rule)
coverage_sweep.reason: Three fallbacks keep the shipped code path exactly: blank level with no result, a run without a CCV on both sides, and spike recovery when spike or parent is a non-detect. Their inputs are values the SOP does define (readings, SOP-5 amounts, SOP-6 pass). No guard or qualifier outside the SOP was added.
fix.patch touches only files under app/src/metalquant, and solve.sh changes nothing else.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A negative first blank followed by blank results: the non-detect is excluded and the mean covers only readings >= mdl. With all blanks non-detects, the shipped first-blank reading is kept.
Blank level 2.5 and a sample reading of 7.0 at dilution 1000: amount is (7.0-2.5)*1000, and the flag is judged on 4.5 against mdl and loq, not on the amount.
Spike and parent both exactly on mdl count as results and use the /added formula. An ND parent or an ND spike falls back to /(added*dilution) using the SOP-5 amounts.
A failed CCV after a sample bracketed by a passing CCV before gives false. A sample after the last CCV uses the nearest-before pass under the new rounding rule. A batch with no CCV gives true.

Replacing the origin-forced fit with the intercept fit changes every reading. Flags and result status are then derived from those readings with no extra tolerance, so a value exactly on a limit is judged by the plain >= and < comparisons.
